questions.q: What is the main advantage of a "train-the-trainer" approach over direct training for a large user population?
options: It requires no documentation at all
It scales faster by training super users deeply, who then train their own departments
It eliminates the need for role-based training
It replaces the need for UAT
questions.explain: Train-the-trainer scales faster than having the implementation team personally train every end user, and it builds the depth super users need for Tier 1 support.

questions.q: Why is training scoped by role rather than taught as a general tour of every screen?
options: Because a specific role, like an AP clerk, only needs deep training on what that role actually does in the system
Because Oracle requires role-based training by contract
Because general training is faster than role-based training
Because role-based training removes the need for documentation
questions.explain: Role-based training mirrors the security model: a role needs training on what it actually does, not a tour of functionality it will never touch.

questions.q: What is knowledge transfer, as distinct from end-user training?
options: The same thing as end-user training, just renamed
A type of Service Request
The deliberate process of making internal staff capable of supporting and maintaining the system without the implementation partner
A step in the fit-gap analysis process
questions.explain: Knowledge transfer specifically prepares internal staff to handle Tier 2 support work — troubleshooting, defect logs, Service Requests — independent of the implementation partner.

questions.q: What is "reverse shadowing" in a knowledge transfer process?
options: Internal staff watching the implementation team work
An Oracle Service Request escalation
A type of regression test
The implementation team watching and coaching internal staff as they do the work themselves
questions.explain: Reverse shadowing flips the roles: internal staff do the work while the implementation team observes and coaches, before stepping back entirely.
